## 💱 Any currency

Pocket Sense is no longer dinars only. Pick your currency in **Settings → General → Currency**, or on the welcome screen when you first set up the app: Jordanian dinars or any of 27 others, from SAR and AED to USD, EUR and INR. Each uses its usual decimals (2 for USD, 0 for JPY), and amount fields follow them. Requested in #7.

- It's one currency for all your data, with no exchange rates, so the app stays offline. Switching relabels your amounts; it doesn't convert them.
- Backups carry the currency, and importing one switches to it.

## 🏪 Merchants

- **Settings → Merchants** adds, renames and deletes the places you pay or get paid by.
- In the transaction and recurring forms, the merchant field searches them as you type. If nothing matches, tap **Create it** to add the name to the list. It stays selected in the field.
- Renaming a merchant updates the entries that use it. Deleting one only removes it from the list; your entries keep the name.
- After the update, the list starts with the merchants already on your transactions and recurring items.

## ✨ Also new

- **What's new:** the first time the app opens after an update, it shows what changed since the version you last used (#5).
- New installs get a **Coffee** category. Existing ones can add it in **Settings → Categories**.

## 🔧 Fixes

- **Clearing a merchant, category or note while editing now saves.** Before, an emptied merchant came back after saving, and switching an edited expense to income kept its expense category. This also applied to recurring items.
- Amount fields only take numbers. Latin and Arabic-Indic digits both still work.
- Charts are easier to read: tooltip amounts are white on the dark tooltip, and pie labels turn dark on light slices.

## Syncing two devices

Update both. A device on 2.3.0 can't sync with one on an earlier version; the app tells you to update both to the same version. Two devices also need the same currency to sync.

## Download
**Android**
- Also on **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/ace.software.pocketsense/)**, which keeps it updated. It ships these same signed APKs, so you can switch between the two and keep your data.
- **`PocketSense-v2.3.0-arm64-v8a.apk`**: almost all modern Android phones. Use this one if unsure.
- `PocketSense-v2.3.0-armeabi-v7a.apk`: older 32-bit phones
- `PocketSense-v2.3.0-x86_64.apk`: emulators and Chromebooks

Installs as an update over any earlier version and keeps your data.

**Linux (x86_64)**: pick one.
- **Debian, Ubuntu, Mint:** `PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.deb`
  ```sh
  sudo apt install ./PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.deb
  ```
- **Fedora, openSUSE:** `PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.rpm`
  ```sh
  sudo dnf install ./PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.rpm   # or: sudo zypper install
  ```
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it.
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.3.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`. Unpack it and run `./PocketSense/pocket_sense`.

All need glibc 2.35 or newer and a running keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet). With the AppImage or the tarball you also need GTK 3, and `parecord` for voice entry (`pulseaudio-utils` on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora, `libpulse` on Arch).
